shouldFix.title: The G10 provenance role denies the platform-copy act that v4 performs
shouldFix.measurement: basedOn.g10OccupancyV2.role says: 'sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v4 does not copy those platforms into fixture directories.' That is false for this successor. authorityClaim says one catalog member is copied onto four D-002 platforms; d002PlatformsQuotedFromG10OccupancyV2.copiesAuthored is true; namedCases[FC-OUTFAIL.no-committed-run].copies and authoredCatalog.members[0].copies each enumerate the four platform paths; and the frozen v2 corpus contains exactly those four platform directories and files. The predecessor v3 role used the same no-copy predicate when v3 had only the non-platform v1 source file, so changing only the speaker to v4 left a stale predecessor statement across the copy-authoring delta.
shouldFix.whyShouldFix: This is a direct false statement about the central purpose of the successor inside the authority-provenance block. A later recording should not simultaneously say that v4 authors the four per-platform copies and that v4 does not copy onto fixture directories. The machine-readable copy lists, physical bytes, primary authority claim, and scope boundaries are otherwise consistent, so this is a SHOULD-FIX rather than a custody or semantic MUST-FIX.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Replace the false final sentence of basedOn.g10OccupancyV2.role with an accurate affirmative statement that sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v4 copies the D-297 no-committed-run implementation onto the four quoted G10 platform tokens under fixtures/sarif-fc-outfail.v2/. Preserve that G10 is only the quoted platform source, that v4 neither occupies G10 nor invents a D-002 platform list, and do not mutate either fixture corpus or close OBL-FC-OUTFAIL-FX.

decision: REJECT — 0 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX. The subject and all four platform copies retain correct custody; the quoted platform order, source equality, D9 witness, non-closure, and non-SATISFIED boundaries hold.
